note:
ISO 2026-W13 runs from March 23 through March 29. Saturn and Neptune are separated by about 2.6° in geocentric ecliptic longitude at the Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Naked eye:** 🌓 First Quarter — 19:17:43 UTC. Moderate moonlight makes timing and local sky position important for faint targets. Use Suhail, Miaplacidus, Aspidiske, α Lyn, Markeb, Alphard as the week’s fixed-sky framework.

**Planets:** Moon: Naked eye; magnitude -8.5; direct motion; 19.8% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Jupiter in ecliptic longitude Mar 26 12:57 UTC. Conjunction with Uranus in ecliptic longitude Mar 23 05:39 UTC. Mercury: Naked eye; magnitude 0.8; direct motion; 28.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Venus: In solar glare; magnitude -3.9; direct motion; 95.1% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Mars: In solar glare; magnitude 1.2; direct motion; 99.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Ceres: Telescope; magnitude 9.1; direct motion; 99.2% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Jupiter: Naked eye; magnitude -2.3; direct motion; 99.1% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Mar 26 12:57 UTC. Saturn: In solar glare; magnitude 0.9; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Solar conjunction in ecliptic longitude Mar 25 08:55 UTC. Uranus: Binoculars; magnitude 5.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Conjunction with Moon in ecliptic longitude Mar 23 05:39 UTC. Neptune: In solar glare; magnitude 7.8; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot. Pluto: Substantial telescope; magnitude 14.6; direct motion; 100.0% illuminated. Below the horizon at 21:00 local apparent solar time, 45°N. Monday 00:00 UTC snapshot.

**Binoculars:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified for binocular observing this week.

**Small telescope:** NGC 2775: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; NGC 2867: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; MCG 9-16-5: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance; NGC 2903: consult its dedicated finder and observing story for equipment guidance

**Substantial telescope:** No fixed-sky Calendar object is classified as requiring a substantial telescope this week.

story_candidates.dek: Suhail is a star in Vel; its declination determines which latitudes can observe it.
story_candidates.body:
Its catalogue position is approximately right ascension 9h 07m and declination -43.4°. These reference coordinates describe its sky location; they are not an observing time or a current altitude.

At the almanac’s default latitude of 45° N, this star rises and sets, reaching approximately 2° altitude at upper culmination. These are geometric calculations from declination, excluding refraction and local obstructions. Darkness and the time of culmination must still be checked for the observing date and your location.

How to find it: Establish the preserved Vel constellation figure from its labeled reference stars, then use the target’s plotted position rather than searching for an isolated star.

Sources: Star Almanack’s stored fixed-object and expanded Bayer catalogues; accepted constellation figures and guiding-star routes. Visibility limits are original geometric calculations from catalogue declination, not weekly predictions.
